full_judgment: "But on perusal of the judgment of the High Court Division it is found that learned Advocates of both the parties who appeared they were confused between the period of subsistence of a usufructuary mortgage and the period of limitation in the case of a suit for redemption of a mortgaged land. The maximum period for which a usufructuary mortgage can be entered into was fifteen years under section 95 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. But by Ordinance No. XXI of 1969, section 95 was amended and thereby the maximum period for a usufructuary mortgage was reduced to seven years. And unless earlier redeemed by repayment of the consideration a mortgagor acquires right to redemption on the expiry of the maximum period of seven years, and if the mortgager does not voluntarily restore possession of the land to the mortgagor, the latter may file a suit for redemption within a period of 60 years from the date of accrual of his right of redemption. In this case the suit was filed just on the accrual of the right of redemption and, as such, it is not barred by limitation.
